question: A stack trace points to a null check missing in a single function inside one file, and the fix is a one-line conditional. Which workflow best matches the scope of this change?
options: A) Split the one-line fix into a multi-phase plan with a separate research session and a separate implementation session afterward
B) Delegate the fix to an Explore subagent so the discovery work stays fully isolated from the rest of the main conversation entirely
C) Direct execution, since the change is a well-scoped, single-file fix with a clear cause already identified from the trace
D) Plan mode, since any production bug fix always warrants a written proposal and a full approval cycle no matter how small the change is
correct_answers: C) Direct execution, since the change is a well-scoped, single-file fix with a clear cause already identified from the trace
explanations: Breaking a one-line, already-diagnosed fix into multiple phases adds unnecessary process overhead for a change this small.
The Explore subagent isolates verbose discovery output for large investigations; there is no substantial discovery phase here since the cause is already known from the trace.
Correct. A single-file fix with a clear, already-identified cause is a well-understood, well-scoped change, which is exactly what direct execution is suited for.
Plan mode is for tasks with multiple valid approaches or architectural implications; forcing every bug fix through it adds friction without benefit when the fix and cause are already clear.
